newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chief Executive says CS Group has critical mass.
newsitem.headline: Chief Executive says CS Group has critical mass.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group has critical mass in its four reorganised core businesses and sees no need to acquire or sell off activities, new chief executive Lukas Muehlemann told a Swiss newspaper on Wednesday.
Muehlemann, in office since the reorganisatiion took effect at the start of this year, told the daily Basler Zeitung his main priority now was implementing the new strategy.
Asked about stock market rumours that he would make big changes at CS Group as he had when he started as CEO of Swiss Reinsurance in 1994, Muehlemann said the two companies were very different.
"At the Credit Suisse Group, on the other hand, we have a very workable platform, critical mass everywhere and the prerequisites with the new structure for long-term success," he said.
"Of course I cannot fully rule out the possibility that we will take advantage of opportunities if they arise," he said.
"But I do not see any need for action based on the current structure," he added.

Muhlemann said Swiss Re , in contrast, had been divided when he arrived between a well-positioned reinsurance side and a less well-placed direct insurance business, which he then sold off to raise capital for expanding reinsurance.
Muehlemann declined to comment directly on another batch of recent market rumours that CS Group planned a closer alliance or merger of some kind with Swiss Re or Swiss insurer Winterthur .

CS Group has some product and marketing cooperation deals with Swiss Re and Winterthur. Speculation of farther-reaching plans has been fueled by the fact that Muehlemann came from Swiss Re and was a colleague of the new Winterthur CEO, Thomas Wellauer, when both were still at McKinsey & Co in Zurich.
"It is better if we do not comment on the rumours," Muehlemann said.
"There are apparently no more limits to imagination these days," he added.
Muehlemann denied yet another recent market rumour that CS Group planned to put all its extensive information tehcnology in the hands of an outside compnay.
CS Group was reorganising its information technology on a decentralised basis, giving each business unit responsibility for its own computing and information needs, Muehlemann said.
"There will be no outsourcing of the entire information technology side," Muehlemann told the paper.
Muehlemann said case-by-case deals with outside information vendors would be easier under the new structure.

"As we recently told our employees -- and this may be a reason for the rumours -- we are restructuring our information technology by applying what we have already established in management organisation. We are decentralising it," he said.
